title: Nvidia Brings Back Jensen Huang as CEO; Shares Surge 31% in Record Rally
excerpt: Nvidia's board voted unanimously Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as president and CEO, 11 days after announcing his resignation.
content:
Nvidia's board voted unanimously Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as president and chief executive, effective immediately — 11 days after the company announced his resignation — and the market responded with one of the biggest single-day rallies in the company's history.

The board had accepted Huang's resignation on Nov. 11, and the company announced it Nov. 12. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named interim CEO, and Harvey C. Jones became board chair. On the Nov. 17 earnings call, Jones said the board had “unanimously accepted” Huang's resignation and “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” Six days later, the board reversed course.

After “a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang,” the board said it was “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang's candor and ability to lead NVIDIA,” had “received input from senior levels of the United States government” and is “confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk.” Jones said the board believes the return is “in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers.”

President Donald Trump said on CNBC on Nov. 23 that he spoke to the board “directly and indirectly” and “I convinced them. I made the deal.” He also said on Truth Social that the board “has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO,” adding “The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA.” Vice President JD Vance led weekend calls to the board, according to CNN and the Wall Street Journal. Trump also said Attorney General Todd Blanche confirmed the government has no evidence Huang engaged in unlawful conduct.

Reports said Huang had two extramarital affairs — one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials probed as a possible Chinese intelligence asset, and one with a direct subordinate at Nvidia. Huang has acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife and apologized. China has denied the espionage allegations. No criminal charge against Huang has been reported.

Nvidia shares closed Monday at $165.05, up $39.52, or 31.48%, from Friday's $125.53 close — the stock's best day since May 2003, adding roughly $952 billion in market value. The S&P 500 closed at 7,237.17, up 4.73%, or 326.78 points, its best day since April 2025. The Nasdaq Composite closed at 24,089.56, up 6.51%. The Dow rose 3.01% to 49,595.31.

Scrutiny of Huang and Nvidia continues. Huang is scheduled to testify at an open Senate Banking Committee hearing on Thursday, Dec. 3, at 10 a.m. ET, titled “Protecting America's AI Advantage: Oversight of U.S. Export Controls,” as the sole witness. Committee chair Sen. Tim Scott (R-S.C.) confirmed the hearing Nov. 23. Huang and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter will also appear for closed-door transcribed interviews Dec. 1 and Dec. 2 with the House committees on China, Intelligence and Foreign Affairs. The Securities and Exchange Commission is probing Nvidia's accounting practices, the Justice Department is reviewing Nvidia's $12.9 billion Hugging Face deal and broader antitrust questions, and California Attorney General Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena on Nov. 19. Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company whose former executive is Alice Huang, was added to the U.S. trade blacklist on Nov. 23. Nvidia's board has formed a committee to investigate whether foreign intelligence targeted Huang and is searching for a new chief compliance officer.

Nvidia is the world's most valuable chipmaker and a bellwether for the artificial-intelligence trade, so the rally lifted the broader market, including the index funds held in many retirement accounts.
